payload.feature:
Fix the recurring linked-worktree Git metadata blocker in Brokkr's DSH implementation lane.

Observed on 2026-09-08: runs close-issue-218-doctor-probes-a--71197022 and close-issue-221-muninn-s-two-res-2f692419 finished implementation and reported runnable checks green, then returned blocked because git add/commit could not create an index.lock under the parent repository's .git/worktrees/<name>. The DSH harness mounts the root read-only and only the seat workspace writable. Its danger-full-access escalation had no approval channel. The operator manually committed the artifacts as 243b1f3 and dbe6e4a. The same defect was already described in docs/essays/one-job-three-hires.md. Fix the delivery integration rather than repeating that workaround.

This fixing run intentionally lives in a standalone clone with its own .git so you can commit the fix. Preserve that clone and commit unsigned. Do not push, open a PR, launch additional Brokkr runs, modify global provider configuration, disable sandbox protections globally, or change the four existing issue worktrees.

Read docs/house-rules.md, decisions 0004/0005, applicable 0043/0046 boundary rulings, the DSH driver implementation and tests. Measure the installed DSH sandbox and permission interface from its CLI/source before selecting a mechanism; do not invent flags. Distinguish DSH's harness-owned sandbox from Brokkr's namespace hands. The defect reproduced here is the former.

Deliver a supported, bounded path for a DSH work-class implementer to stage and create an unsigned commit in a genuine linked Git worktree. Resolve git-dir/common-dir through Git, supporting spaces and nested paths and respecting read-only seats. Preserve unrelated-path, credential, hook, protected-config, and sibling-worktree restrictions under the declared boundary; do not blindly mount the whole parent checkout or shared .git writable. If a safe implementation requires a semantic choice beyond accepted authority, write a focused proposed decision and identify the exact question instead of silently weakening the boundary. Consider a scoped commit mechanism or explicit supported write roots only where the actual harness can enforce them. Surface actionable refusal early when support is unavailable, rather than burning an implementation before discovering it cannot commit.

Add behavioral regression evidence with a real linked worktree: stage and unsigned commit succeeds under the real supported DSH sandbox mechanism; parent/sibling sentinel files and protected hooks/config remain unwritable; ordinary standalone repositories still work. Prove driver argv/config plumbing separately as needed. Fake CLI tests alone do not establish the sandbox behavior. Do not call real DSH probes with unlimited model loops. Keep tests/builds to CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 and RUST_TEST_THREADS=2. Record any unavailable live evidence explicitly. Frozen contracts, production policy, reference, and evaluator corpus stay unchanged; add versions if needed and reconcile measured pins.

Update the relevant guide and a proposed decision for any new semantics. Run fmt, clippy, workspace tests, both self and verify bundle compilation, and exact coverage per house rules. Distinguish host tests from nested-box skips; do not claim exact coverage from an ordinary test pass. Commit completed code/tests/docs and report precise limitations. This run owns the durable fix only; delivery of the four original issue branches remains with the operator/controller.


FINAL LANDING REVIEW. Prior repair run fix-the-recurring-linked-worktre-4362947b completed at 624510ee360d3220975026c57246e1cb0c0e508f with no remaining security finding. The controller merged shipped main 5bc8cf305aaef9af269866cbf83f094939691399 and clarified low-severity staged-content and non-fast-forward limitations in the guide and proposed 0054. Current clean candidate 66110ef, following final review of aa179f3. Review the combined final candidate, preserve the entire original scope above, and remediate material findings if any. Do not re-open already-proven historical findings without new evidence.

The private common store is reclaimed before any trusted Git read; own-branch promotion uses a pre-seat baseline and CAS, connectivity/fsck-checked fetch and unique temporary ref. Shared refs, existing objects, config, sibling worktrees must remain protected. Commit within the same seat is supported; staged-but-uncommitted objects/private stashes are not delivered, documented as a low-severity limitation. No implication that host history corruption by shallow was reproduced: controller probes did not reproduce it, while commondir config redirection WAS reproduced and the reclaim fixes it.

The controller ran final host gates with TMPDIR=/var/tmp, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, RUST_TEST_THREADS=2, BROKKR_REQUIRE_BOUNDARY_EVIDENCE=1. Consult .forge/controller-final-validation.json and .log for actual head-bound results, including the unmodified exact coverage script; do not infer coverage from ordinary tests or obsolete logs. If you change production bytes, obtain new candidate-bound coverage (or explicitly flag pending controller execution); no fabricated gate. Other relevant evidence is .forge/implement-store-reclaim-evidence.md, .forge/controller-2769ec8-redirection-probe.json, .forge/controller-dsh-installed-interface-source.json. The remote decision registry was checked by the controller and has no 0054 collision. All four original issue fires #218/#219/#221/#231 are merged. Publication of this fix remains controller-owned after this final run: no actor push/PR/merge. Report precise residuals, completed checks, and a clean committed final head.


FOLLOW-UP LANDING at 66110ef. Final landing run fix-the-recurring-linked-worktre-4a9f4470 completed and confirmed the whole scope and all gates, with two residuals: low security hardening because --args FD was opaque to the bind scanner, and info because recovery docs omitted a possible leftover anchor. The controller removed --args from the accepted profile table, added refusal assertions (including writable_binds rejecting the full profile), and clarified both the guide and proposed 0054. --ro-bind-fd remains accepted because it grants no write; it does not expand options like --args. These are the only follow-up changes. Revalidate those fixes and their interaction with the full scope; do not reopen documented staged-only limitations without new evidence. The controller has refreshed .forge/controller-final-validation.json/.log on 66110ef. Read that actual proof, and preserve the head if clean. Publication remains controller-owned.


CI PORTABILITY FOLLOW-UP at f4c2243. Run fix-the-recurring-linked-worktre-e2a53602 completed at 3d8a95d, with full host gates passing and one INFO manual-recovery-text residual. PR #250 is published; remote Windows job 102356190246 failed compilation because Unix PermissionsExt and symlink were not cfg-gated. Controller f4c2243 guards restore_access and its call with cfg(unix), guards the two Unix-specific tests, and closes the INFO residual by explicitly removing/rebuilding objects/info in the failure message, guide and proposed 0054, with an assertion. No Linux behavior or original scope was narrowed. A Windows-target cross-compile `cargo check --locked -p brokkr-protocol --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` exited 0 (.forge/controller-windows-check.log); it is compile evidence, not Windows runtime evidence. Controller has refreshed full host gates at this head in .forge/controller-final-validation.json/.log. Review these precise deltas and interaction with the original scope, preserving a clean head if passed. Remote native Windows and all PR checks remain required after controller publication of this completed run. Do not push or open a second PR.


REPAIR ALL REMOTE CI FAILURES BEFORE DELIVERY. Current local clean commit f4c2243 fixes Windows compilation and the last INFO recovery-text residual, but is NOT pushed. PR #250 still names 3d8a95d. Local Windows-target protocol all-targets compile passes; native Windows runtime evidence still pending. The completed GitHub workflow 34317329778 has THREE additional failures, which this repair must address while preserving the full original security requirement and literal coverage gate:

1. macOS two new reclaim tests compare canonical Git paths with noncanonical tempfile paths: /private/var/folders/... versus /var/folders/... at original lines1438 and1581. Compare canonical identities; do not skip supported-platform tests simply to make them green.
2. Linux exact coverage executes its unique target binaries under /tmp/forge-coverage. fixture_root() unconditionally returns None when current_exe's parent starts with /tmp, and BROKKR_REQUIRE_BOUNDARY_EVIDENCE correctly turns the skip into a failure. Root host proof had TMPDIR=/var/tmp and thus passed. Make the real proof usable on ordinary CI without dropping its outside-/tmp requirement, changing scripts/coverage-exact.sh, weakening the strict evidence gate, or depending solely on a controller TMPDIR convention. A genuinely separate temporary root outside the profile tmpfs is appropriate.
3. Ubuntu native test second boxed session fails after trusted promotion: an existing shared loose object path disappeared (original test line2490). Determine whether the trusted fetch's automatic Git maintenance/repacking moved it, or whether the boundary actually let the seat destroy it; reproduce the relevant case. Shared existing objects must remain protected; DO NOT delete/weaken the before/after sentinel assertions or redefine success as ref names unchanged. Git fetch on this host advertises --no-auto-maintenance and --no-auto-gc. Disabling trusted promotion's automatic maintenance may be appropriate if that is the measured cause, but do not guess away a real boundary failure.

Full logs: .forge/controller-ci-windows.log, controller-ci-macos.log, controller-ci-ubuntu.log, controller-ci-coverage.log. Preserve the frozen contract/policy/reference/fixtures, original full scope, proposed decision0054, and commit unsigned. Controller is rerunning f4c2243 host gates now; the file will show finished/head binding before this run is launched. Any further source change needs fresh exact gate evidence and final review. Fix, verify, review, and close out; no actor publication. Controller will update existing PR250 with final commit and completed run, rerun all native platform/coverage CI, and only merge green.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```
